title: fix(superheroes): the review panel reads the session's model from its transcript when the start event omits it
body:
Closes #2110.

## What's changing, and why

When a session's start event did not name the model it runs on (headless builders, and many compact or resume events), the review panel treated the host model as unknown. That made every native Claude reviewer ineligible, so a panel that could have seated Claude dropped it and disclosed `host-model-unknown`, even though the session's own transcript records the model on every turn. Now, when the start event names no model, the panel reads it from the session's own transcript, counting only turns written since this start and never a subagent's. A panel therefore keeps its Claude seats whenever any record of the model exists. A model from an earlier start still never stands in for the live one, and a session the launcher spawns never inherits its parent's model. Review also caught, and this PR fixes, a crash path its first version added: a transcript path that UTF-8 can't encode no longer aborts the session-start hook before it removes the reviewer pass from later shells.

## What we're accepting

- **The bite-proofs were produced by the build orchestrator, not the implementer** (disclosed degradation): the harness refused the implementer's proof command, so the orchestrator ran every proof itself. All eight guarded elements went red with their guard removed and green with it restored. Nothing is unproven.
- **The fixer wrapper differed from the emitted order** (disclosed degradation): the review loop's fixer got its order as a pointer to the driver-emitted file, not as pasted text. The order itself was unchanged.
- **Session 3 has no review record of its own** (disclosed degradation): it converged on `0d21b530`, then a CI-only rename moved the head before its record was written. Session 4 reviewed the final head with a full panel, and its record carries every earlier finding.

## How to see it

N/A, nothing to see: this is review machinery. The change shows only in a review's seat map: no `host-model-unknown` and a known host family when the start event omits the model.

## Advisor vet

<!-- superheroes:advisor-vet -->

**Verdict: NOT-READY** · 58cacc626f18e3183c1f2ae41c51312569876119 (vet 633: the review record and a catch-up with main are owed)

**What was checked.** Both problems from the last vet are fixed. I checked each one myself on this Mac:
- The test that broke on a Mac now passes there. If the bug it guards comes back, the test still fails.
- The reader test now catches a reader that picks an older model over the latest one. Before, that mistake passed every test.
- This round changed tests only; no shipped code changed.
- The other tests this PR touches also pass on the Mac.

**Why it is not ready.**
- The re-check of the fix by an independent reviewer happened, but nothing durable records it. The only trace is a sentence in the builder's comment. The review record, the account every merge rests on, still describes the previous commit.
- Since the PR was built, two other PRs merged and touched the same release-notes file. So the PR can't merge until it catches up with them.

Both are routine. The builder catches up, gets one independent reviewer to read the fix and the catch-up together, writes the record, and hands back. No code changes.

**What accepting it means.** Once that lands: nothing beyond what the PR says. Reviews keep their Claude reviewers when a session's start event leaves the model out. Consuming projects owe nothing. The leftover finding that used to be on your list is fixed, and the new record will say so.

**What is yours to decide.** `None`.

Full vet: [vet 633 receipt](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2113#issuecomment-6378971747)

### Follow-ups for the advisor

Follow-ups: 3 (0 owner-call)

- FU1 [info] The cloud setup leaves the uv cache without the repo's dev dependencies, so a sandboxed implementer cannot run `scripts/pinned-python -m pytest` offline until the builder fills the cache from its own shell (this build did so before WO-1b).
- FU2 [info] Resolved in `e3f0c9c9` (vet 632 ruled it craft; one dispatch). It was review session 4's Minor: in `test_host_model_2110.py`, the transcript-reader test's malformed and invalid-UTF-8 lines sit before the qualifying line, so the backward scan never reaches them. A fix would reorder the fixture so those lines are scanned first. Stopped by the third-rework tripwire on that file.
- FU3 [defect] Break-it tests that carry a credential-shaped fixture reach the run step with the value replaced by a bare `[REDACTED]` token, so they fail with `NameError` before exercising the code (sessions 2 and 4 here). Either the redaction should keep a runnable literal or the break-it run should read the unredacted text.

- **Bite-proof producer.** Promised: the implementer produces the proof and the orchestrator re-runs it. Delivered: the orchestrator produced and ran G1–G4, E1 and G6 and wrote the record (WO-3's implementer did produce G5), because the harness refused the implementer's proof command. - **Fixer order delivered by pointer.** Promised: the emitted fixer order text is the dispatch prompt. Delivered: a two-line wrapper pointing the fixer subagent at the driver-emitted order file (sha256 recorded); the order itself was not changed.
- **Session 3 record not written.** Promised: every terminal review session writes its record. Delivered: session 3 converged on `0d21b530`, but the WO-4 CI fix moved the head before the record, so session 4 re-reviewed the final head and its record carries the account.
